title: Effect of Sintering Temperature on the Microstructure and Integrated Properties of MgAlTiVFeCo Lightweight High-Entropy Alloy

recollection.starting_material: Mg–Al–Ti–V–Fe–Co high-entropy alloy powder mixture (likely gas-atomized or mechanically alloyed elemental powders)
recollection.intervention: Consolidation by pressure‐assisted sintering (probably spark-plasma or hot-press) while systematically varying the sintering temperature, e.g. 800–1100 °C
recollection.structure: Temperature-dependent mixture of BCC (or dual BCC1/BCC2) solid solutions with some FCC or intermetallic/oxide precipitates; higher temperatures give larger grains and higher relative density
recollection.mechanism: Rising temperature enhances diffusion and promotes solid-solution formation and densification; excessive temperature causes grain growth and possible formation of brittle intermetallics, so properties show an optimum at mid-range temperature
recollection.results: Best overall properties around ≈1000 °C: >98 % theoretical density, hardness ≈300–350 HV, compressive yield strength ≈900–1100 MPa with plastic strain >15 %; lower temperatures leave residual porosity and lower strength, whereas highest temperatures reduce hardness/strength through grain coarsening

score.note: Correctly identifies pressure-assisted/SPS-like sintering and the optimum near 1000 °C. The structure discussion is generic and partly speculative, missing the specific uniformly distributed AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3 barrier phases. The mechanism mentions diffusion and densification but omits the passive-film/Cl− blocking corrosion mechanism and parabolic, biphasic oxidation kinetics. The optimum temperature and density estimate are reasonably close, but the hardness is drastically underestimated (300–350 HV versus 1235.5 HV), and the reported strength/ductility values are unsupported.
